blocks.title: Track indices, references and call depth separately
paragraphs: Arrays provide a fixed number of indexed elements. Reliable array algorithms need a valid index range and a clear processed portion. Recursion adds another dimension: each call has its own progress measure and local state.

blocks.title: Traverse exactly the valid indices
paragraphs: For an array of length n, valid indices are 0 through n−1. A standard index loop uses i < values.length, not i <= values.length. An empty array has length zero and no valid element; a null reference does not refer to an empty array.

Use an enhanced for loop when only element values are needed. Assigning to a primitive loop variable does not replace an array element; use indices when the operation must write back to particular positions.

blocks.title: Give every loop a processed-prefix meaning
paragraphs: To count positives, initialize count=0 and add one whenever the current element is >0. To find the first target, return as soon as a match is found and return -1 only after the whole array has been searched. Declare how duplicates and a missing target are handled.

For filtering into a temporary array, maintain a separate output count: positions below that count contain selected values in input order. Allocate an exact-length result and copy the filled prefix if the result must have no spare cells. The input index and output count need not advance together.

blocks.title: Assignment copies a reference; array copying is explicit
paragraphs: int[] b = a makes b refer to the same array. b[0] = 9 then changes an element visible through a. By contrast, cloning a primitive array copies its elements into another array. Reassigning b afterward does not reassign a.

Copying an array of object references copies those references, not each referenced object. A new outer array can therefore still share its mutable element objects. Decide which level of independence the operation requires.

blocks.title: Prove a base case is reached
paragraphs: For prefixSum(values, length), require 0 ≤ length ≤ values.length and a non-null array. At length0, return0 without reading an element. Otherwise add values[length−1] to the result for length−1. The non-negative length decreases, so a valid call reaches the base case.

Unwind results in reverse call order. A missing base case, unchanged argument or excessive call depth can cause StackOverflowError; mathematical termination is different from a promise that arbitrarily deep recursion fits memory. The example uses small ints so sum overflow is not an issue.

blocks.title: An alias and a copy feed a recursive sum
paragraphs: The first line is 2 9 8. The recursive call reads the shared array a after its second element became9, so the sum is17. Its call lengths are3,2,1,0; the base result0 accumulates2, then9, then6.

blocks.title: Check empty, shared and boundary cases
paragraphs: For each algorithm, state the input contract, valid index interval and processed-prefix invariant. For copying, name the level being copied. For recursion, state the base case and a decreasing measure before tracing output.

cards.prompt: Why is i <= values.length wrong for a loop that reads values[i]?
cards.answer: The last valid index is values.length−1. At equality, values[i] is out of bounds. The usual bound is i < values.length.

cards.prompt: Are an empty array and null equivalent?
cards.answer: No. An empty array exists and has length0. null does not refer to an array, so accessing its length or an element fails.

cards.prompt: Why does an array-filter loop need an output count separate from the input index?
cards.answer: Only selected input values are written. The input index advances every iteration, while the output count advances only when a value is retained.

cards.prompt: When may first-index search safely return -1 for an absent target?
cards.answer: After it has inspected all allowed positions without finding a match. Returning -1 after the first nonmatching element misses later matches.

cards.prompt: What is different between int[] b = a and int[] b = a.clone()?
cards.answer: Assignment shares the same array. clone creates a distinct array containing copied primitive elements, so changing b’s elements does not change a’s.

cards.prompt: Does copying an array of object references also copy its objects?
cards.answer: No. The new array contains copied references to the same objects. Independent element objects require an additional, deliberately defined copying operation.

cards.prompt: What two obligations make a recursive prefix sum terminate for a valid input?
cards.answer: A base case handles length0, and each non-base call decreases a non-negative length by one. Reading length−1 must occur only when length>0.

cards.prompt: Why can a mathematically terminating recursive method still fail for a very large input?
cards.answer: Each call consumes finite runtime resources. A sufficiently deep chain can exhaust the call stack even when its argument decreases toward a base case.

guided.title: Filter safely and trace a recursive prefix
guided.prompt: Specify and outline keepPositive(int[] values), returning a new array of positive values in input order without mutating the input. Use {-1, 3, 0, 3} and the empty array as checks. Then trace prefixSum({2, 9, 6}, 3) and state its precondition.

fields.label: Filter algorithm with valid index bounds and output count
Recursive calls, base case and returned values

rubric: Keeps both occurrences of3 and rejects0.
Returns an independent array and handles empty input without reading an element.
Explains the filled output prefix and separates it from the input index.
States the prefix length contract and traces lengths3,2,1,0 before unwinding.
reference: Count positive values, allocate exactly that length, then fill the new array; alternatively use a bounded temporary buffer and copy its filled prefix. The example returns {3,3}; the empty input returns an empty array.
No assignment writes into the input array. Returning the original reference would not satisfy the new-array requirement even when every value is positive.
For prefixSum, require non-null values and 0≤length≤values.length. The results at lengths0,1,2,3 are0,2,11,17.
